shape.text: The key is the prefix phx_ followed directly by a random body, with no separator inside the body and no checksum. The provider's key-generation code in its repository, last read at the pinned revision, defines the prefix and the generator.

Body length and alphabet depend on the generation date, and keys of every era can still be live because rotation is optional. Since 2026-03-30 the body is 48 or 49 characters from a base57 alphabet (base62 without 0, 1, O, I and l). Until then it was a 35-byte base62 body of at most 48 characters; earlier still a 32-byte base62 body of at most 43 characters.

Across the eras a key therefore has 42 to 49 letters and digits after the prefix. About 1.6 percent of the oldest keys render at 42 characters; shorter renderings are under 0.03 percent of any era. The per-length shares are derived from the generator algorithm, not observed.

One scanner rule reads this key as phx_ plus 43 to 48 letters, digits and underscores, which misses 49-character base57 bodies and 42-character base62 bodies and admits an underscore the generator never emits; it is not used to narrow the band.
A run of 50 or more characters after the prefix, or a key directly attached to a letter, digit, underscore or hyphen, is not a key.

unresolved.reason: Treating a key attached to an identifier character as not a key, and a run of 50 or more characters as not a key, are project boundary choices, not provider statements.

issuance.text: The provider's documentation describes the phx_ personal API key; it acts as the user across every organization the user can reach.
No PostHog personal API key was issued or observed for this record.

unresolved.reason: No key was issued for this research; an optional check of one key issued today would be expected to be 48 or 49 characters with none of 0, 1, O, I and l.

collisions.text: The phc_ project token is public by design (the documentation says it is fine to be public) and is not a secret.
The earliest personal keys had no prefix and were 43 characters of URL-safe Base64; they have no distinguishing anchor.
